body.input: Which AI companies opened an office in Germany in 2026?

response.content:
Based on available information, here are AI companies that opened or established offices in Germany in 2026:

## **OpenAI**
OpenAI established a presence in **Munich and Berlin** in 2026. The company is actively hiring for multiple roles based in Munich and Berlin (including Applied AI Engineers, Strategy & Operations, Regional Client Partners, and Engineering Managers), operating on a hybrid model with 3 days per week in the office and offering relocation assistance to new employees.

## **Agile Robots**
Munich-based AI robotics company **Agile Robots** opened a new factory in **Fürstenfeldbruck** (near Munich) earlier in 2026. The facility can produce up to 10,000 humanoid robots annually. The company, now valued at $8.5 billion after a $500 million funding round led by SoftBank and Nvidia, is expanding its production capacity in Germany.

## **Polarise**
**Polarise**, an AI infrastructure company, expanded its footprint in Germany in 2026. In addition to its existing Munich location (where it converted a former bank data center in Tucherpark into an AI factory), the company announced plans to build new AI data center facilities ("AI factories") in **Bavaria, Hesse, and North Rhine-Westphalia**, with the first phase of new capacity expected to come online in early 2027. Polarise aims to add approximately 150 megawatts of AI computing capacity in Germany by end of 2028.

---

These are the specific cases identified from available reporting. The broader trend in 2026 shows Germany attracting significant AI investment, particularly in industrial/physical AI and AI infrastructure, though a comprehensive list of every AI company that opened a German office during the year may not be fully captured here.

Polarise described expanding its AI capacity in Germany in 2026, including converting a former bank data center in Munich and planning new AI factories in Bavaria, Hesse, and North Rhine‑Westphalia, showing the company’s German footprint grew that year.

# German AI robotics start-up valued at $8.5 bn after new fundraising

AFP

2 min read

 9984.T

  -3.04%

  +0.63%



 

German AI robotics start-up Agile Robots said Thursday that a new funding round valued the company at $8.5 billion (7.7 billion euros), providing additional firepower for a global expansion.

One of Europe's leading makers of humanoid robots and robotic arms, Agile works in the field of "physical AI", with its equipment used to automate and speed up factory work. [...] Earlier this year it opened a factory outside Munich that it says can produce up to 10,000 humanoid robots annually to meet rising demand.

Agile Robots is among a crop of start-ups in Germany trying to shift AI from the digital realm into the physical world, with a particular focus on its deployment among the country's traditional manufacturers.

While Europe has lagged behind the United States and China in developing the best-known artificial intelligence models, deployment of AI in industrial processes is an area where some believe the continent could have an edge.

But when it comes to robotics, European firms face fierce competition internationally from bigger Chinese rivals such as Unitree, famed for its backflipping robots, which have enjoyed substantial government support. [...] The Munich-based company raised $500 million in the funding round led by the Japanese tech investment giant SoftBank. Other participants included AI chip behemoth Nvidia and the Japanese group Hitachi.

A spokesman told AFP that the company, founded in 2018, was now Europe's most valuable "physical AI" robotics firm.

"Our vision is intelligent robots working alongside people in factories and warehouses everywhere, and Agile Robots is determined to lead that shift," said CEO and founder Zhaopeng Chen.

The funding would be used to support expansion in the United States, additional production capacity in Germany and entry into new markets, he said.

The company says it has deployed around 20,000 robots in industries including automotive, consumer electronics and logistics.

HÜRTH/DÜSSELDORF, November 12, 2026 - Polarise is expanding its AI capacity in Germany by around 150 megawatts by the end of 2028. To do so, Polarise is expanding its existing facilities and, in addition to its existing locations in Oslo and Munich, is building new AI factories in Bavaria, Hesse, and North Rhine-Westphalia, which are either already planned or under construction. The first phase of the new capacity will be delivered as early as the beginning of 2027 and then significantly expanded over the course of the year, so that by the end of 2028, a total of around 150 megawatts of sovereign computing power will be brought online. In doing so, Polarise is contributing to the German federal government’s goals of at least fourfold increase in AI computing capacity in Germany by 2030. [...] “In Germany, ‘hidden champions’ are traditionally the companies upon which entire industries are built,” says Daniel Abbou, Managing Director of the German AI Association. “For AI, that means infrastructure, because without powerful and sovereign data centers, there can be no AI ‘Made in Germany.’ Polarise is building precisely this infrastructure - quickly and without sealing new land - making decisive progress in advancing Germany as an AI hub.”

## The Backbone of Munich’s AI Factory [...] Polarise does not build new data centers on greenfield sites; instead, it sustainably transforms abandoned industrial and data center locations into AI factories. In Munich’s Tucherpark, the company has already converted a former bank data center in just six months - from planning to operation - and has been operating the site ever since. At the heart of this approach are Polarise’s modular AI Pods, self-contained data center units that are integrated into existing buildings. Cooling is provided by the nearby Eisbach River. In the future, the waste heat will be used to heat the surrounding neighborhood. Polarise provides the infrastructure for the Industrial AI Cloud here and also offers capacity for its own AI cloud.
